date_label: Three days at Genoa, on Wilde's journey from the Riviera into Switzerland, recounted in a letter postmarked 20 March 1899 from Gland. The letter dates neither the stop nor the days; the February 1899 placing of that journey is an itinerary inference, not read in the source.
summary: On his way from the Riviera to Harold Mellor's villa at Gland, Wilde broke his journey at Genoa and met a young Florentine actor named Didaco, with whom he spent three days. He reported it to Reginald Turner in a letter postmarked 20 March 1899 - a named, dated, first-person-attested liaison of the exile years, and one of the few for which Wilde records the other man's name. Nothing further about Didaco survives in the correspondence read: the letter ends on the following printed page with no second mention.

sources.quote: On my way I stopped at Genoa, where I met a beautiful young actor, a Florentine, whom I wildly loved. He has the strange name of Didaco. He had the look of Romeo, without Romeo's sadness: a face chiselled for high romance. We spent three days together.
sources.context: Wilde to Reginald Turner, [postmark 20 March 1899], Gland, Switzerland - the closing paragraph on the printed page; the letter continues onto printed 1133 and ends there without returning to Didaco.
sources.supports: The whole of the record: Wilde's account of meeting Didaco at Genoa, of loving him, and of three days spent together
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 1178, printed folio 1132 confirmed on rendered page.
